Bid my private value to win whenever the market price is below my value and avoid leaving expected surplus on the table.]

[Second-price sealed-bid: winner pays the second-highest bid. In private-value settings bidding your value is dominant; given the common-value component, my observed value (20) is my best estimate of my utility. Bidding 20 avoids the winner’s curse in expectation and maximizes expected surplus: if I win I earn value minus second price. No past history and only one round, so bid truthfully at 20.]
